name: Career Readiness & Networking

objectives.text: Identify different careers connected to agriculture, food, and natural resources in the local community
Sort agricultural careers into the AFNR career pathways such as animal systems, plant systems, agribusiness, and food products and processing
Describe the qualities and employability skills employers look for in an agricultural job candidate
Interview an agricultural professional about their career path and summarize what they learned
Write a simple resume that lists SAE, FFA, and school experiences
Match potential AFNR career opportunities with personal interests, talents, goals, and preferences using a career interest inventory
Explain how agriculture, food, and natural resources industries contribute to society and the economy and create career demand
Categorize the education, certification, and training requirements for careers in each AFNR pathway
Prepare a professional resume, cover letter, and portfolio that document SAE records and FFA achievements for a specific agricultural position
Demonstrate professional interview skills in a mock job interview for an agricultural career
Explain how AFNR businesses use human resources functions to recruit, train, evaluate, and retain employees
Develop a professional network plan that includes mentors, employers, alumni, and industry contacts made through SAE and FFA
Demonstrate professional networking practices such as introductions, follow-up communication, and online professional profiles at an industry or FFA event
Analyze the steps needed to advance within a chosen agricultural career and set goals for continuous growth
Evaluate job, internship, or postsecondary opportunities and justify a chosen career pathway based on SAE and FFA experience

changes: Kept all six original objectives, rewording some. The grade 4 objective now names AFNR careers in the local community, the grade 6 objective adds employability skills, and the grade 10 interview objective now uses the verb demonstrate. Added objectives for sorting careers into pathways, interviewing a professional, career interest matching, AFNR economic scope, categorizing credential requirements, building a cover letter and portfolio, human resources practices in AFNR businesses, applied networking practice, and career advancement goal setting. Standards are mapped only from grade 9 up. The FFA emblem, FFA mission, SAE definition, and FFA importance standards were left unused because they are not about career readiness.
